content.text:
I submitted **index 23** (Ca 0.14, Co 0.70, Mn 0.16). It was the only sample of the three I measured that gave a positive photocurrent, and that current is tiny (3×10⁻⁸ A). I can't tell whether it's close to the best composition in the 183-sample library.

**What I measured:**
- **Photocurrent:** the budget was 3 measurements, so I used one on each corner of the composition spread.

  | Index | Region | Photocurrent |
  |---|---|---|
  | 23 | Co-rich | +3×10⁻⁸ A |
  | 103 | Mn-rich | −1×10⁻⁸ A |
  | 41 | Ca-rich | −2.2×10⁻⁷ A |

  Both negative results mean no useful photoanode response.
- **XRD (4 of 5 used):** samples 23, 103, 41 and a central one, 91, all showed the same main crystal phase (strongest peak at Q≈2.79 Å⁻¹). Only small extra peaks differed: one in the Co-rich sample (Q≈2.56) and one in the Ca-rich sample (Q≈1.16). So XRD didn't help pick which samples to measure for photocurrent.

The small positive signal suggests the best compositions are probably high in Co. With the budget used up, I couldn't test Co-rich samples near index 23 (such as 26, 9 or 6) to confirm that. They would be the first to measure in any follow-up.
